name: Vireo Analytics – Cookieless WordPress Stats & Google Analytics Alternative
author: RebelCode

sections.description:
Vireo Analytics shows who visits your WordPress site and where they came from. It’s a cookieless, privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative that keeps visitor data in your own database.

Black Friday: 60% off Vireo Pro

Every Pro plan is 60% off for the first year until 1 December. Get Vireo Pro at 60% off.

Switch from Google Analytics and keep your history

Import your past traffic from Google Analytics 4, Jetpack Stats, Koko Analytics, WP Statistics, Burst Statistics, Independent Analytics, Statify, SlimStat, Post Views Counter, Matomo, Plausible, Fathom Analytics, Simple Analytics, Cloudflare Web Analytics or Clicky. Your charts carry on from the day you switch, with no day counted twice. The switching guides show what comes across from each tool.

See the Google searches behind every post

Connect Google Search Console and each post’s stats list the searches it showed up for, with clicks, impressions and average position.

Track visits from ChatGPT and other AI assistants

ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot each show as a traffic source. Next to the readers they send, Vireo counts how often their crawlers fetched your pages. The AI visibility scan checks whether AI crawlers can read your site and says how to fix anything that blocks them.

Real visitors only

Vireo keeps crawlers, SEO tools, uptime monitors and AI bots out of your numbers and shows how many it removed. If a visit you expected is missing, Settings, Troubleshooting tells you why. The bot directory lists every bot it filters.

More free features

  • An Overview that opens with what changed and why, then top pages, referrers, countries and devices.
  • Time on page, bounce rate and Core Web Vitals from real visitors.
  • Form submissions from Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, Ninja Forms, Formidable, Forminator, Fluent Forms, Jetpack Forms and other form plugins, plus custom events, link clicks and 404s.
  • A Popular posts block, widget and shortcode, an email digest and CSV export.
  • Headless WordPress: count visits on an Astro, Next.js or static front end with one script tag. Free for one connected site; Pro adds more.
  • Ask Claude, Cursor or another AI assistant about your traffic through the built-in MCP server and REST API.
  • Read-only dashboard access for editors and clients, and multisite support.
  • Available in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Dutch, Portuguese and Russian.

Vireo Pro

For stores, campaigns and client reporting:

  • Revenue from WooCommerce, Easy Digital Downloads, FluentCart and Freemius, credited to the page and source that brought each buyer, with goals and funnels.
  • Orders and revenue for each UTM campaign, QR codes, short links and affiliate clicks.
  • Heatmaps of where visitors click and scroll.
  • Scheduled email reports and client dashboards with your logo.
  • A live view, entry and exit pages, and on-site search analytics.
  • The pages AI assistants send readers to, and weekly checks on what ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini say about your site.

Pro starts at $69 a year for one site, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. Get Vireo Pro.

Privacy

Vireo stores nothing on visitors’ devices. It recognises a returning visitor for one day only, using a scrambled code that resets every night, and it honours Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control. Visitor data never leaves your site. The only outside services are the ones you choose to connect, listed under External services below.

External services

Vireo never sends visitor data anywhere. It contacts the services below only when you set them up, and each one pulls data into your site. A site that imports nothing, connects nothing and downloads no geolocation database contacts none of them.

Once an hour the plugin sends a request to its own tracking endpoint to check it still works. That request stays on your server and carries no data about anyone.

WordPress.com Stats API (Jetpack Stats importer)

Used only while you run the Jetpack Stats import. On a site connected to Jetpack it calls https://public-api.wordpress.com/rest/v1.1/sites/{site ID}/stats/ with the site ID, signed by Jetpack’s connection. With an API key it calls https://stats.wordpress.com/csv.php with that key and the site address. Each request also carries a date range and report name. Provided by Automattic Inc.: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Google Analytics Data API (importer)

Used only while you run the Google Analytics import. Sends your service account’s credentials to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token and a date range to https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com. Provided by Google LLC: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Cloudflare Web Analytics (importer)

Used only while you run the Cloudflare import. Sends your API token, account ID, website and a date range to https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/graphql. Provided by Cloudflare: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Matomo (importer)

Used only while you run the Matomo import. Sends your auth token, site ID and a date range to the Matomo Reporting API at the address you entered. For a self-hosted Matomo that’s your own server. For Matomo Cloud, the Matomo privacy policy applies.

Fathom Analytics (importer)

Used only while you run the Fathom import. Sends your API token, Fathom site ID and a date range to https://api.usefathom.com/v1/aggregations. Provided by Fathom Analytics: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Simple Analytics (importer)

Used only while you run the Simple Analytics import. Sends your API key, the website’s hostname and a date range to https://simpleanalytics.com/. Provided by Simple Analytics: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Clicky (importer)

Used only while you run the Clicky import. Sends your site ID, sitekey and a date range to https://api.clicky.com/api/stats/4. Provided by Clicky: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Google Search Console

Used once you connect Search Console. Sends your service account’s credentials, the property address and a date range to https://searchconsole.googleapis.com, once a day and whenever you press refresh. A refresh fetches the last week first, then older history in fortnight-sized requests over a few minutes. This is the plugin’s only recurring outside call, and disconnecting stops it. Provided by Google LLC: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Google PageSpeed Insights

Used only when someone presses the PageSpeed button. Without an API key, the button opens https://pagespeed.web.dev/ in that person’s browser and the server sends nothing. With an API key added under Settings, the server calls https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed with the page address, the device to test as, the admin’s language and the key. Results are kept for a day. Provided by Google LLC: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

DB-IP (geolocation)

Used only when you press the download button for the geolocation database. The request for the monthly file from https://download.db-ip.com carries no site or visitor data, and lookups then run on your own server. DB-IP Lite data is provided by DB-IP under CC BY 4.0: Website, Privacy Policy.

MaxMind GeoLite2 (geolocation)

Used once you save a MaxMind account ID and license key under Settings, Geo-location. The plugin sends them to https://download.maxmind.com to download the GeoLite2 Country database, then checks once a day for a newer file. Lookups run on your own server. This product includes GeoLite2 Data created by MaxMind, available from https://www.maxmind.com, used under the GeoLite End User License Agreement. Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins, Add New, search for “Vireo Analytics” and install it.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Vireo Analytics, Overview. Your first pageviews show up within a minute.

To bring your history across, go to Vireo Analytics, Settings, Import data. If another analytics plugin is installed, the Overview offers to import from it.
sections.faq:
Is there a paid version?

Yes, Vireo Pro. Everything above the Vireo Pro list is free. Pro adds revenue reports, goals and funnels, client dashboards and more connected sites. If you stop paying, the free plugin keeps working with all your data. See pricing.

Is Vireo Analytics GDPR compliant?

Vireo is built for it. It uses no cookies or browser storage for tracking, and it scrambles visitor details with a code that resets every 24 hours. Raw IP addresses are never written to the analytics tables. With Shorten IP addresses on, it meets the IP rule in the French regulator CNIL’s guidance on analytics without consent. Whether your site needs a banner is for you and your adviser to decide, and you should still mention the plugin in your privacy policy.

What does the “Visitors” number mean?

Visitors is a unique count for each day. Longer ranges show the total of daily visitors, because the code that recognises a visitor resets every night and nothing links today’s visit to tomorrow’s. Pageviews are exact over any range.

Does it honour Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control?

Yes, by default. Visitors whose browser sends DNT: 1 or Sec-GPC: 1 aren’t recorded. Developers can change this with the vireo_honor_opt_out filter.

Why are my numbers lower than another plugin’s?

Many analytics plugins count uptime monitors, SEO crawlers and AI crawlers as visitors. Vireo filters them out and shows what it removed, by category, so you can check the difference. The vireo_bot_ua_pattern filter changes what counts as a bot.

How do I switch from Google Analytics?

Go to Settings, Import data. Vireo reads the Google Analytics Data API with a service account key and your numeric property ID (not the G- measurement ID), and brings across daily pageviews and visitors, pages, referrers, countries, devices, outbound clicks, downloads, form submissions and custom events.

How do I switch from Jetpack Stats?

Go to Settings, Import data. On a site connected to Jetpack there’s nothing to fill in. Otherwise paste your WordPress.com API key and site address. Daily pageviews, top posts and referrers come across. Imported days show pageviews, which is what Jetpack Stats records.

How do I switch from Plausible Analytics?

Export your site in Plausible (Site settings, Imports & Exports), then upload the zip under Settings, Import data. Pageviews, visitors, pages, referrers, countries, devices, goals and custom events come across. No API key is needed.

How is it different from Google Analytics?

Vireo runs on your own WordPress site, sets no cookies and sends nothing to Google. It answers the questions most site owners ask: how many people visited, what they read, where they came from and on what device. Your Google Analytics history can come with you.

Can I ask an AI assistant about my stats?

Yes. Vireo runs an MCP server at /wp-json/vireo-analytics/mcp. Open Settings, Search Console & API and copy the ready-made configuration for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or another MCP client. The assistant signs in with an application password, sees only what that user can see, and can only read. No outside service sits in between.

Can I see Vireo stats in MainWP?

Yes, with Vireo Pro.

Can I show my most popular posts?

Yes. Use the Popular posts block, the [vireo_popular_posts] shortcode or the Popular posts (Vireo) widget. Pick the number of posts, the period, the post types, and whether to show images and view counts. For a single post’s views, use the Post views block or [vireo_views].

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The tracker runs on every page load, cached pages included. Every page tracks once your cache refreshes after activation.

How do I track a custom template or landing page?

The tracker loads through wp_footer(). If a theme or page builder template leaves that call out, add <?php do_action( 'vireo_print_tracking_script' ); ?> just before </body> in that template. It only prints once, so it’s safe on pages that also call wp_footer().

Does it work with headless WordPress (Astro, Next.js)?

Yes. Under Settings, Other sites, enter your front end’s address and paste the script tag shown there into every page. It follows Astro view transitions, and data-spa="history" covers other single-page front ends. Each pageview is matched to the WordPress post at the same path, so per-post views and Search Console data work as they do with a theme.

Does it track logged-in admins?

Your own admin visits are left out by default. Turn on admin tracking under Vireo Analytics, Settings to include them.

How long is data kept?

Visitor hashes are rolled up into daily totals after 24 hours. Daily totals are kept for two years by default; change it under Settings, Retention.

Will it slow down my site?

No. Vireo records the visit after the page has loaded, through a small handler that skips your plugins and theme.
sections.changelog:
0.31.1

  • New: Settings > General > Views column picks the period the Views column on the Posts and Pages screens covers: the last 7, 30 or 90 days, or all time. Sorting by the column follows the same period. Developers can set any number of days with the vireo_posts_column_days filter.

0.31.0

  • Change: buttons, form controls and the admin screens follow the WP RSS Aggregator v5 admin style, so Vireo sits next to it without a visual break.
  • Change: the Astro install snippet and the update notice name the @jgnpm/vireo-astro package, translated in all nine languages.

0.30.1

  • Translations: every string added in 0.30.0 is translated in all nine languages, including the new Other sites and Troubleshooting settings tabs.

0.30.0

  • Change: the top of the Overview is one card: the headline and its cause, the AI read when Pro is active, then the week’s facts. On wide screens the week sits beside the headline.
  • New: What changed leads with the channels (Search, Other sites, Direct, AI assistants, Social, Email) as before and after, biggest change first, each opening to the sites that moved. Pages and sources that moved follow on one shared scale, small moves fold into one line, a page published in the period is listed as new, and suspected junk referrers are left out.
  • New: every card header names the range it covers, with both periods’ dates on hover. The range and filters stay pinned under the admin bar while scrolling, as one chip naming the range on phones and tablets.
  • New: referrers show the source’s logo from a bundled icon set, with nothing fetched from outside the site. Browsers and operating systems get theirs too.
  • Change: today is drawn as a day still in progress: a dashed last segment on the sparklines, a lighter bar marked “so far”, and Average daily traffic over complete days only.
  • Change: the daily chart’s scale fits the current period; a prior-period day above it is marked at the top instead of shrinking every bar.
  • Change: Top countries is a table with flags, changes and visitors. Technology shows device types, browsers and operating systems side by side.
  • Change: a share that moved by a point or more shows its change as a percentage with an arrow, and the tooltip spells out the points and the earlier share.
  • New: the dashboard widget switches its 7, 30 and 90 day figures between pageviews and visitors and remembers the choice, draws today lighter, and folds www. into the bare host in its referrer list.
  • New: a Shopify store can be a connected site. Choose A Shopify store when you connect it and Vireo gives you a custom pixel to add under Settings, Customer events in the Shopify admin; the store’s visits show on the dashboard under its own name. The pixel sets no cookies, keeps nothing in the browser and sends no customer details. It also sends completed checkouts, which Vireo Analytics Pro adds to Revenue as orders.
  • New: links from your pages to a connected Shopify store carry the page they were clicked on, so Pro can credit a store order to the post that sent the buyer.
  • Fix: with Automatic, the visitor’s address is read from Cloudflare’s CF-Connecting-IP only when the request came through Cloudflare. Behind any other proxy on the same server or network it follows X-Forwarded-For from the nearest hop back, and X-Real-IP is read only when you pick it.
  • Fix: country headers other than Cloudflare’s are believed only from proxy ranges you name with the vireo_geo_trusted_proxies filter, and Cloudflare’s only from Cloudflare.
  • New: a Proxy addresses setting next to Visitor IP source. A named header such as X-Forwarded-For is now believed only when the request arrives from a private network, Cloudflare or an address listed there, so a visitor reaching the server directly can’t choose their own address. Sites behind another CDN should add its ranges.
  • Fix: the daily pageview limit per address treats an IPv6 network (/64) as one address.
  • Fix: the daily limit on new pages applies to pages that aren’t a real post, and a post ID only earns the per-post allowance on that post’s own address. Site Health says when the limit is reached and how to raise it with the vireo_max_new_paths_per_day filter.
  • Fix: pages of a connected site count against the daily limit on new pages like the site’s own.
  • Change: the email sent when recording stops is on for new installs. Sites that were already running keep it off until they turn it on under Settings.
  • Fix: when Jetpack Stats is turned off, the Jetpack import says to turn it on while the import runs, in place of WordPress.com’s raw error.
  • Fix: All time opens with the total and the day it starts from, and a range before Vireo started recording says so with the date, in place of the new-install “Collecting data” line.
  • Change: Settings has two new tabs. Other sites holds connected sites and the headless front end, and Troubleshooting holds “Why wasn’t my visit counted?” and the bot filter test, so Tracking is only about what gets counted. Links to the old places still open the right tab.
  • Fix: the Privacy check’s “Open setting” links stay on one line.

Earlier versions are listed in changelog.txt in the plugin folder.
